papers.name: Paper 1 The study of religions: beliefs, teachings and practices

topics.name: Buddhism
points: Beliefs: the Dhamma and dependent arising
Beliefs: the Three Marks of Existence (anicca, anatta, dukkha)
Beliefs: human personality (five skandhas; sunyata and Buddha-nature)
Beliefs: human destiny (Arhat and Bodhisattva ideals, Buddhahood, the Pure Land)
Beliefs: the life of the Buddha (birth, upbringing, Four Sights, ascetic life, Enlightenment)
Beliefs: the Four Noble Truths (dukkha, samudaya and the Three Poisons, nirodha and nibbana)
Beliefs: the Eightfold Path and the Threefold Way (ethics, meditation, wisdom)
Practices: places of worship (temples, shrines, viharas, gompas) and puja
Practices: meditation (samatha, vipassana including zazen, visualisation of Buddhas and Bodhisattvas)
Practices: death and mourning rituals in Theravada communities, Japan and Tibet
Practices: festivals and retreats in Great Britain: Wesak and Parinirvana Day
Practices: Buddhist ethics: kamma and rebirth; karuna and metta
Practices: the five moral precepts and the six perfections

topics.name: Christianity
points: Beliefs: nature of God (omnipotent, loving, just), the problem of evil, the Oneness of God and the Trinity
Beliefs: creation and the roles of the Word and Spirit
Beliefs: the afterlife: resurrection, judgement, heaven and hell
Beliefs: the incarnation and Jesus as Son of God
Beliefs: the crucifixion, resurrection and ascension
Beliefs: sin (including original sin); salvation through law, grace and Spirit; atonement
Practices: liturgical, non-liturgical and informal worship; private worship; prayer
Practices: sacraments: baptism (infant and believers') and Holy Communion
Practices: pilgrimage (Lourdes and Iona) and celebrations (Christmas and Easter)
Practices: the role of the church in the local community (food banks, street pastors)
Practices: mission, evangelism and church growth
Practices: the worldwide Church: reconciliation, persecution, and CAFOD, Christian Aid or Tearfund

topics.name: Catholic Christianity
points: Beliefs: one God as Trinity: scriptural origins and the Nicene Creed
Beliefs: creation (Genesis 1 and 2), human dignity and humanity's relationship with creation
Beliefs: the incarnation: Jesus fully God and fully human, the divine Word
Beliefs: redemption: life, death, resurrection and ascension of Jesus; salvation through grace
Beliefs: the afterlife: resurrection, judgement, heaven, hell and purgatory
The seven sacraments: meaning of sacrament and the sacramental nature of reality
Sacraments: Baptism, Confirmation and Reconciliation
Sacraments: Anointing of the sick, Matrimony and Holy orders
Sacraments: the Eucharist as source and summit of Christian life
Practices: prayer (formal and informal) and the Lord's Prayer
Practices: popular piety (Rosary, Stations of the Cross), pilgrimage and the funeral rite
Practices: love of neighbour and Catholic social teaching (Gaudium et Spes 26); justice, peace and reconciliation
Practices: CAFOD, Trocaire and Missio; mission and evangelism
Practices: Society of St Vincent de Paul; Corrymeela community or Pax Christi

topics.name: Hinduism
points: Beliefs: Brahman (nirguna and saguna) and the three features of the divine
Beliefs: divine presentations: the Tri-murti, male and female deities, avatara
Beliefs: cosmology: prakriti, tri-guna, maya, the four ages and many worlds
Beliefs: atman, samsara, karma and moksha
Beliefs: free will, suffering, knowledge and ignorance; personal virtues (ahimsa, respect, empathy, self-control, humility, love)
Beliefs: the four aims of life and the meanings of dharma (sanatana and varnashrama dharma)
Practices: places of worship and forms of worship (havan, puja, arati, darshan, bhajan/kirtan, japa)
Practices: Shaivism and Vaishnavism; focuses of worship including murti
Practices: festivals in Great Britain: Diwali and Holi
Practices: the four paths of yoga
Practices: pilgrimage; Varanasi and Kumbh Mela
Practices: environmental projects including cow protection; charities for well-being, social inclusion and women's rights

topics.name: Islam
points: Beliefs: the six articles of faith (Sunni) and five roots of Usul ad-Din (Shi'a)
Beliefs: Tawhid (Surah 112) and the nature of God
Beliefs: angels, including Jibril and Mika'il
Beliefs: predestination, human freedom and the Day of Judgement
Beliefs: Akhirah: life after death, resurrection, heaven and hell
Beliefs: Risalah: Adam, Ibrahim and Muhammad
Beliefs: holy books: the Qur'an, Torah, Psalms, Gospel and Scrolls of Abraham
Beliefs: the Imamate in Shi'a Islam
Practices: Five Pillars of Sunni Islam and Ten Obligatory Acts of Shi'a Islam
Practices: Shahadah
Practices: Salah (including Jummah) and differences between Sunni and Shi'a prayer
Practices: Sawm during Ramadan and the Night of Power
Practices: Zakah and Khums
Practices: Hajj
Practices: Jihad: greater and lesser jihad
Practices: festivals in Great Britain: Id-ul-Adha, Id-ul-Fitr and Ashura

topics.name: Judaism
points: Beliefs: the nature of God (One, Creator, Law-Giver and Judge, loving and merciful) and the Shekhinah
Beliefs: the afterlife: judgement and resurrection
Beliefs: the Messiah
Beliefs: the Covenant with Abraham and the Promised Land (Genesis 12:1-3)
Beliefs: the Covenant at Sinai and the Ten Commandments (Exodus 20:1-17)
Beliefs: key moral principles (justice, healing the world, charity, kindness) and Pikuach Nefesh
Beliefs: free will and the 613 mitzvot
Practices: the synagogue: importance and design features; Orthodox and Reform synagogues
Practices: public worship, the Amidah and Shabbat
Practices: home worship, private prayer and the Tenakh and Talmud
Practices: rituals: Brit Milah, Bar and Bat Mitzvah, marriage and mourning
Practices: dietary laws (kosher and trefah)
Practices: festivals: Rosh Hashanah, Yom Kippur and Pesach

topics.name: Sikhism
points: Beliefs: the Mool Mantra and the nature of God; God as Creator
Beliefs: human life as an opportunity to unite with God; karma, rebirth and mukti
Beliefs: the five khands and barriers to liberation
Beliefs: gurmukh and manmukh; haumai
Beliefs: oneness of humanity and equality, including of women
Beliefs: sewa (tan, man, dhan) and sangat
Practices: the gurdwara: features and role in the community
Practices: prayer at home, akhand path and nam japna
Practices: langar as an expression of sewa
Practices: festivals: Vaisakhi, Divali and Gurpurbs in India and Great Britain
Practices: visiting historical gurdwaras, including the Golden Temple
Practices: birth and naming ceremonies; the names Singh and Kaur
Practices: Amrit Sanskar, the Khalsa and the five Ks; sahajdhari and amritdhari Sikhs

topics.name: Theme A Relationships and families
points: Human sexuality: heterosexual and same-sex relationships
Sex before and outside marriage
Contraception and family planning
The nature and purpose of marriage; same-sex marriage and cohabitation
Divorce and remarriage; ethical arguments (sanctity of vows, compassion)
The nature and purpose of families; same-sex parents and polygamy
The roles of men and women; gender equality, prejudice and discrimination

topics.name: Theme B Religion and life
points: Religious teachings on the origins of the universe; the Big Bang theory
The value of the world: stewardship, dominion, responsibility and awe
Use and abuse of the environment: natural resources and pollution
Use and abuse of animals: animal experimentation and animals for food
Origins of human life: religious teachings and evolution
Sanctity of life and quality of life
Abortion, including ethical arguments
Euthanasia
Beliefs about death and the afterlife and their impact on beliefs about the value of life

topics.name: Theme C The existence of God and revelation
points: The Design argument
The First Cause argument
The argument from miracles
Arguments against the existence of God: evil and suffering; science
Special revelation: visions; enlightenment
General revelation: nature and scripture
Ideas about the divine: omnipotent, omniscient, personal, impersonal, immanent, transcendent
The value of revelation and enlightenment; alternative explanations

topics.name: Theme D Religion, peace and conflict
points: Peace, justice, forgiveness and reconciliation
Violence, violent protest and terrorism
Reasons for war: greed, self-defence and retaliation
Just war theory and holy war
Pacifism
Religion as a cause of conflict
Nuclear weapons, nuclear deterrence and weapons of mass destruction
Religion and peace-making; responses to victims of war

topics.name: Theme E Religion, crime and punishment
points: Good and evil intentions and actions
Reasons for crime: poverty, upbringing, mental illness, addiction, greed, hate, opposition to unjust law
Views on people who break the law; hate crimes, theft and murder
Aims of punishment: retribution, deterrence and reformation
Treatment of criminals: prison, corporal punishment and community service
Forgiveness
The death penalty, including ethical arguments (utility, sanctity of life)

topics.name: Theme F Religion, human rights and social justice
points: Prejudice and discrimination in religion, including women and same-sex relationships
Freedom of religion and religious expression
Human rights and responsibilities; social justice
Racial prejudice and discrimination; positive discrimination
Wealth: attitudes and uses; responsibilities of wealth
Exploitation of the poor: fair pay, excessive interest, people-trafficking
Responsibilities of those living in poverty; charity

topics.name: Theme G St Mark's Gospel: the life of Jesus (textual study)
points: John's preparation (1:1-8) and Jesus' baptism and temptation (1:9-13)
The paralysed man (2:1-12) and Jairus' daughter (5:21-24a, 35-43)
The rejection at Nazareth (6:1-6) and the feeding of the five thousand (6:30-44)
Caesarea Philippi (8:27-33) and the Transfiguration (9:2-9)
Passion prediction (10:32-34) and James and John's request (10:35-45)
Bartimaeus (10:46-52) and the entry into Jerusalem (11:1-11)
The Last Supper (14:12-26) and Gethsemane (14:32-52)
The trials before the Jewish authorities (14:53, 57-65) and Pilate (15:1-15)
The crucifixion and burial (15:21-47) and the empty tomb (16:1-8)
Significance: titles of Jesus for 1st-century Jews and 21st-century Christians
Significance: Jesus as teacher and miracle worker; historicity of miracles
Significance: the Last Supper, death and resurrection; authority of Mark's Gospel

topics.name: Theme H St Mark's Gospel as a source of religious, moral and spiritual truths (textual study)
points: Parables of the sower (4:1-9, 14-20), growing seed (4:26-29) and mustard seed (4:30-32)
Jesus and the children (10:13-16), the rich man (10:17-27) and the greatest commandment (12:28-34)
The man with leprosy (1:40-45) and the call of Levi (2:13-17)
The Syro-Phoenician woman's daughter (7:24-30) and the epileptic boy (9:14-29)
The widow at the treasury (12:41-44) and the anointing at Bethany (14:1-9)
The call of the first disciples (1:16-20) and the woman with a haemorrhage (5:24b-34)
The mission of the Twelve (6:7-13) and the cost and rewards of discipleship (8:34-38; 10:28-31)
Peter's denials (14:27-31, 66-72) and the commission and ascension (16:14-20)
Significance: the Kingdom of God (present, future, inner, communal)
Significance: Jesus' attitudes to those disregarded by society, then and now
Significance: discipleship and faith; authority of Jesus' teaching
